class.name: MidiOut
class.brief_description: Sends MIDI output to hardware and software MIDI ports.
class.description:
[MidiOut] provides real-time MIDI output functionality using RtMidi. It lets you open physical MIDI ports or create virtual MIDI ports to send MIDI messages to synthesizers, DAWs, and other MIDI-capable software.
Use the static methods [method get_port_names] and [method get_port_count] to discover available MIDI output ports before opening a connection. Messages are sent immediately via [method send_message] once a port is open.

method.name: open_port
method.description: Opens a MIDI output port by its index number. Port indices are zero-based and can be determined using [method get_port_names] or [method get_port_count]. Returns [constant OK] on success, [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if [param port_number] doesn't exist, [constant ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] if a port is already open, [constant ERR_CANT_OPEN] if no ports are available or the port could not be opened, or [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE] if MIDI output could not be initialized. [codeblock] var err = midi_out.open_port(0) if err != OK: print("Could not open MIDI output: ", error_string(err)) [/codeblock]

method.name: open_virtual_port
method.description: Creates and opens a virtual MIDI output port with the specified name. Other applications can connect to this port to receive MIDI messages you send. The port name is shown in the MIDI port lists of other applications. Virtual ports are only supported on macOS, iOS and Linux. On Windows, Android and other platforms this returns [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE]; on Windows, create a virtual port with a loopback driver such as loopMIDI and open it with [method open_port] instead. Returns [constant OK] on success, [constant ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] if a port is already open, or [constant ERR_CANT_OPEN] if the port could not be created.

method.name: close_port
method.description: Closes the open MIDI output port, regular or virtual. After closing, open another port before sending additional MIDI messages. Returns [constant OK], or [constant ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST] without printing an error if no port was open.

method.name: is_port_open
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if a MIDI output port, regular or virtual, is currently open, [code]false[/code] otherwise.

method.name: get_port_count
method.description: Returns the number of available MIDI output ports on the system.

method.name: get_port_name
method.description: Returns the name of the MIDI output port at the specified index. Returns an empty string if the port index is invalid.

method.name: get_port_names
method.description: Returns an array containing the names of all available MIDI output ports on the system.

method.name: send_message
method.description: Sends a raw MIDI message. The [param message] should contain the complete MIDI packet (e.g. status byte and data bytes). Returns [constant OK] on success, [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] if [param message] is empty, [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] if no port is open, or [constant FAILED] if the MIDI driver reported an error while sending.

signal.name: midi_error
signal.description: Emitted when RtMidi reports an error or warning. [param error_type] is one of the [enum MidiError] constants, and [param error_message] is a human-readable description. If nothing is connected to this signal, the error is printed to the console instead. Once you connect to it, handling the error is up to you. Errors caused by invalid method arguments are always printed and reported through return values, not this signal.
